definitions.gloss: to chase; to run after; to pursue
definitions.explanation: To run after someone or something in order to catch them. Used for physical pursuit of people, animals, or objects.
To pursue something abstract such as a dream, goal, or ideal.

examples.japanese: {犬|いぬ}が{猫|ねこ}を{追|お}いかけた。
{子供|こども}たちが{公園|こうえん}でボールを{追|お}いかけている。
examples.english: The children are chasing a ball in the park.

examples.japanese: {泥棒|どろぼう}を{追|お}いかけて{捕|つか}まえた。
examples.english: I chased the thief and caught him.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}い{頃|ころ}は{理想|りそう}ばかり{追|お}いかけていた。
examples.english: When I was young, I was always chasing ideals.

examples.japanese: {流行|りゅうこう}を{追|お}いかけるのに{疲|つか}れてしまった。
examples.english: I got tired of chasing trends.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound verb formed from {追|お}う (to chase) + かける (to begin/to do toward). More colloquial than {追|お}う alone, and emphasizes the active motion of running after something.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {犬|いぬ}が{追|お}いかける (a dog chases)
- {夢|ゆめ}を{追|お}いかける (to pursue a dream)
- {流行|りゅうこう}を{追|お}いかける (to chase trends)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {追|お}う: to chase, to pursue — more general and also used in written language
- {追跡|ついせき}する: to track, to pursue — more formal, used for investigations or surveillance
